title: NIS 2023 · Paper 2: Solution design
instructions:
Answer all questions.
The number of marks is given in brackets [ ] at the end of each question or part question.

You can write any codes in pseudocode or any other programming language that you studied.

parts.title: Boolean algebra and logic circuit (a)(i)
parts.text:
Consider the following Boolean algebraic expression:

**Q = (NOT A OR B) AND (NOT(A OR NOT(A OR B))).**

Fill in the truth table for the expression.

scheme.mark_scheme:
| A | B | Q |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 0 | 1 | 1 |
| 1 | 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 1 | 0 |

1 mark for each correct row.

Note: The candidate is only required to gain the correct answer (bit) on each row to gain the mark.

Accept working in other order from that shown on the MS.

points.criterion: Correct Q value for A=0, B=0
Correct Q value for A=0, B=1
Correct Q value for A=1, B=0
Correct Q value for A=1, B=1

parts.title: Boolean algebra and logic circuit (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Simplify the given above expressions using the laws of Boolean algebra.

Show your work.

scheme.mark_scheme:
1. (A̅ + B) * NOT(A + NOT(A + B))
2. (A̅ + B) * (A̅ * (A + B))
3. (A̅ + B) * (A̅ * A + A̅ * B)
4. (A̅ + B) * (0 + A̅ * B)
5. (A̅ + B) * (A̅ * B)
6. (A̅ * A̅ * B + A̅ * B * B)
7. (A̅ * B + A̅ * B)
8. (A̅ * B)

1 mark for De Morgan’s law (line 2).
1 mark for Involution/double negation law (line 2).
1 mark for Distributive laws (line 3, 6).
1 mark for Complement law (line 4).
1 mark for idempotent laws (line 7).

Accept other correct solutions.

points.criterion: Correct use of De Morgan’s law
Correct use of Involution/double negation law
Correct use of Distributive laws
Correct use of Complement law
Correct use of idempotent laws

scheme.model_answer: Q = A̅ * B
scheme.ai_instructions: Award marks for valid Boolean algebra working using the listed laws. Accept other correct solutions, but do not award full marks for an unsupported final expression when working is required.

parts.title: Boolean algebra and logic circuit (b)
parts.text:
Write a Boolean expression for the presented circuit.

![Logic circuit with inputs A, B and C and output X. B is inverted, B and C enter an AND gate, those results enter an OR gate, and that result with A enters a NAND gate.](https://icnwfwszbwyewktnnupl.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/media/mocks/nis-2023-p2/q1-logic-circuit.png)

scheme.mark_scheme:
• NOT(A AND (B AND C OR NOT(B)))
or
• ¬(A ∧ (B ∧ C ∨ B̅))

1 mark for B.C.
1 mark for B̅.
1 mark for (B̅ + (B.C)).
4 marks for any completely correct answer from any of the given bullet points.

points.criterion: Correct B.C term
Correct B̅ term
Correct (B̅ + (B.C)) sub-expression
Completely correct final expression including NOT of A AND sub-expression

scheme.model_answer: X = NOT(A AND ((B AND C) OR NOT(B)))

accepted.expression: NOT(A AND ((B AND C) OR NOT B))

parts.text: Explain the differences of using primary and foreign keys in given database.

A primary key pub_ID is used to ensure data in the all tuple of the table Publishers is unique/ pub-ID uniquely identifies a record in the Publishers table (1)

questions.title: Clinic booking system design
questions.text: A small clinic initially used a spreadsheet containing the following columns to record visitors: ID, Client name, Gender, Date of Birth, Phone number, Address, Booking date, Booking time, Speciality, Doctor name. It was decided to create a website where users can book an appointment.

parts.title: Clinic booking system design (a)
parts.text: Describe **two** advantages of the new system.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Easier/faster to book an appointment with a doctor/ more effective communication with clinic (1)

Less wastage of time to book an appointment with a doctor/ not time consuming to book an appointment (1)

More efficient stock management and booking systems (1)

[max 2]

Accept any reasonable answer.

points.criterion: Valid advantage, such as easier/faster booking or more effective communication
Second valid advantage, such as less wasted time or more efficient booking systems
Other reasonable advantage

scheme.model_answer:
1. It is easier and faster for clients to book an appointment with a doctor.
2. It reduces wasted time when booking appointments and improves communication with the clinic.
scheme.ai_instructions: Award a maximum of 2 marks. Accept any reasonable answer.

parts.title: Clinic booking system design (b)
parts.text: Describe the essential characteristics of a user-friendly website.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Effective navigation (1)
Good error handling (1)
Be intuitive/easy-to-use/be predictable (1)
Be able to communicate with the user (1)
Provide the ability to personalize (1)
Be loyal to user errors (1)
Speak the user's language (1)
Giving soft hints (1)

[max 2]

Accept any reasonable answer.

points.criterion: States a valid user-friendly characteristic
States a second valid user-friendly characteristic

scheme.model_answer: A user-friendly website should have effective navigation and be intuitive and easy to use. It should also handle errors well and communicate clearly with the user.
scheme.ai_instructions: Award a maximum of 2 marks. Accept any reasonable answer.

questions.title: Toy store data flow diagram
questions.text:

All data about sold toys (**ToyID, Price, Toy Description**) are stored in the database, **Toy Database**.

• Each toy has a **barcode**.
• A shop assistant scans each chosen toy with a barcode scanner.
• A process, **Generate Bill**, outputs a **Bill** which is presented to the client.
• **Toy Description** and **Price** for each product sold are printed in the bill.

parts.text:

1 mark for ToyID / Barcode.

questions.title: Fact-finding for boat rental system
questions.text:
A boat station provides boats for rent. A boatman keeps track of the time of renting and the return of the boats in a copybook. At the peak of the tourist season there are a lot of queues due to the increase of boat booking. The boatman cannot handle writing the issue time of the rent and accepting payment at the same time. To solve this problem, he hires a programmer to develop a computerized boat rental system.
For each of the following fact-finding techniques, describe how the programmer can use the technique to analyse the current system.

parts.title: Fact-finding for boat rental system (a)
parts.text: interview

scheme.mark_scheme:
ask/talk to the boatman how rental is paid (1)

ask the boatman what info is recorded in the Copybook (1)

ask the customers if they are satisfied with the current system (1)

[max 1]

Accept any reasonable answer.
Accept answers only related to scenario.

points.criterion: Describes a relevant interview use in the scenario

scheme.model_answer: The programmer can interview the boatman to ask what information is recorded in the copybook and how rental payment is handled.
scheme.ai_instructions: Award a maximum of 1 mark. Accept any reasonable answer only if related to the scenario.

parts.title: Fact-finding for boat rental system (b)
parts.text: survey

scheme.mark_scheme:
a series of questions that are answered on paper or on a website from the boatman to find out what he likes/dislikes about the method of recording boat rent (1)

questionnaire customers to find out how much time do they spent waiting in queue (1)

questionnaire customers about payment preferences (1)

[max 1]

Accept any reasonable answer.
Accept answers only related to scenario.

points.criterion: Describes a relevant survey/questionnaire use in the scenario

scheme.model_answer: The programmer can give customers a questionnaire to find out how long they spend waiting in the queue and their payment preferences.
scheme.ai_instructions: Award a maximum of 1 mark. Accept any reasonable answer only if related to the scenario.

parts.title: Fact-finding for boat rental system (c)
parts.text: observation

scheme.mark_scheme:
watch how boatman writes record about rent, charges and gives boat (1)

watch how many customers visit the boat station (1)

[max 1]

Accept any reasonable answer.
Accept answers only related to scenario.

points.criterion: Describes a relevant observation use in the scenario

scheme.model_answer: The programmer can observe how the boatman records rentals, charges customers and gives out boats during busy periods.
scheme.ai_instructions: Award a maximum of 1 mark. Accept any reasonable answer only if related to the scenario.
